title.en: Volume 445 Biographies 232: Wu Kedu, Zhu Yixin, Tu Keshou, An Weijun, Wen Ti, Jiang Chunlin
title.raw: 卷445 列傳二百三十二 吴可读 朱一新 屠可守 安维峻 文悌 江春霖

sentences.zh: 列傳二百三十二

translations.literal: Biographies 232
translations.idiomatic: Biography 232

sentences.zh: 吳可讀潘敦儼朱一新屠仁守吳兆泰何金壽安維峻

translations.literal: Wu Kedu, Pan Dunyi, Zhu Yixin, Tu Renshou, Wu Zhaotai, He Jinshou, An Weijun
translations.idiomatic: [Biographies of] Wu Kedu, Pan Dunyi, Zhu Yixin, Tu Renshou, Wu Zhaotai, He Jinshou, and An Weijun

sentences.zh: 文悌江春霖

translations.literal: Wen Ti, Jiang Chunlin
translations.idiomatic: Wen Ti and Jiang Chunlin

sentences.zh: 吳可讀，字柳堂，甘肅皋蘭人。

translations.literal: Wu Kedu, styled Liutang, was a native of Gaolan in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kedu, whose courtesy name was Liutang, came from Gaolan in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 初以舉人官伏羌訓導。

translations.literal: At first, as a provincial graduate he served as educational instructor at Fuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He first took office as educational instructor at Fuxiang on the strength of his provincial graduate degree.

sentences.zh: 道光三十年，成進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of the Daoguang reign he passed the metropolitan examination, and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1850 he became a metropolitan graduate and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 晉員外郎，遭憂去，主講蘭山書院。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director, but left office on mourning and became lecturer at Lanshan Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice director, he then left office to observe mourning and served as head lecturer at Lanshan Academy.

sentences.zh: 會撒拉番蠢動，被命佐團練。

translations.literal: When the Salar tribesmen stirred up trouble, he was ordered to assist in organizing local militia.
translations.idiomatic: When the Salar tribes rose in unrest, he was ordered to help organize local militia training.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起故官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period ended, he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部郎中，轉御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director in the Ministry of Personnel, then became a censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to a directorship in the Ministry of Personnel and then appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 各國使臣請覲，議禮久未決，可讀請免拜跪，時論韙之。

translations.literal: When foreign envoys requested audience, court ritual was long undecided; Kedu memorialized to exempt them from kneeling and prostration, and public opinion approved.
translations.idiomatic: When foreign envoys sought an audience, court debate over protocol dragged on for a long time; Kedu urged that they be excused from kneeling and prostration, and contemporary opinion sided with him.

sentences.zh: 烏魯木齊提督成祿誣民為逆，擊殺多人，虛飾胜狀，為左宗棠所劾。

translations.literal: Cheng Lu, military governor of Urumqi, falsely charged the people with rebellion, killed many, and fabricated reports of victory; he was impeached by Zuo Zongtang.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Lu, military governor of Urumqi, had falsely branded common people rebels, killed many of them, and padded his reports with fictitious victories, until Zuo Zongtang impeached him.

sentences.zh: 可讀繼陳其罪有可斬者十，不可緩者五，尋逮問，讞上論斬，廷臣請改監候。

translations.literal: Kedu then memorialized that his crimes included ten warranting execution and five that could not be delayed; soon Cheng was arrested and tried, the verdict recommended death, but court ministers asked that it be changed to imprisonment awaiting execution.
translations.idiomatic: Kedu followed with a memorial listing ten capital offenses and five that brooked no delay; Cheng was soon arrested and tried, the case report recommended execution, but ministers at court asked that the sentence be commuted to imprisonment pending execution.

sentences.zh: 可讀憤甚，复疏爭：「請斬成祿以謝甘民，再斬臣以謝成祿。

translations.literal: Kedu was greatly angered and memorialized again in protest: "I beg that Cheng Lu be executed to appease the people of Gansu, and that your servant be executed next to appease Cheng Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Kedu submitted another protest: "I beg that Cheng Lu be put to death to answer to the people of Gansu, and that your servant be put to death in turn to answer to Cheng Lu.

sentences.zh: 」語過戇直，被訶責，鐫三級。

translations.literal: " His words were excessively blunt, and he was rebuked and demoted three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: " His language was judged excessively blunt; he was reprimanded and demoted three ranks.

sentences.zh: 歸，复掌教蘭山。

translations.literal: He returned home and again headed teaching at Lanshan.
translations.idiomatic: He went home and once more took charge of teaching at Lanshan Academy.

sentences.zh: 逾年，穆宗崩，德宗纘業，起吏部主事。

translations.literal: The next year Emperor Muzong died and Emperor Dezong succeeded; Kedu was recalled as a secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, when Emperor Muzong died and Emperor Dezong ascended the throne, he was recalled as a secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年，穆宗奉安惠陵，自請隨赴襄禮。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu, when Muzong was interred at Huiling, he volunteered to accompany the rites and assist in the ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1879, when Emperor Muzong was laid to rest at Huiling, he asked to accompany the funeral procession and assist in the rites.

sentences.zh: 還次薊州，宿廢寺，自縊，未絕，仰藥死，於懷中得遺疏，則請為穆宗立嗣也。

translations.literal: On the return journey he stopped at Jizhou, lodged in an abandoned temple, hanged himself; before he died he took poison; in his bosom was found a final memorial asking that an heir be established for Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: On the way back he halted at Jizhou and spent the night in a ruined temple; he hanged himself, and when that had not yet killed him he took poison and died. A final memorial found on his person asked that an heir be named for Emperor Muzong.

sentences.zh: 其言曰：「罪臣聞治不諱亂，安不忘危。

translations.literal: Its words said: "Your guilty servant has heard that in times of order one does not shrink from speaking of disorder, and in times of peace one does not forget peril.
translations.idiomatic: It read: "Your guilty servant has heard that a well-governed age does not shrink from speaking of disorder, and a secure age does not forget danger.

sentences.zh: 危亂而可諱忘，則進苦口於堯舜，為無疾呻吟，陳隱患於聖明，為不祥舉動。

translations.literal: If peril and disorder may be concealed and forgotten, then offering bitter counsel to Yao and Shun would be feigning illness and groaning, and setting forth hidden dangers before sage clarity would be an ill-omened act.
translations.idiomatic: If peril may be hushed up and forgotten, then offering blunt counsel even to Yao and Shun would count as groaning without sickness, and laying bare hidden dangers before a sage ruler would count as an ill-omened act.

sentences.zh: 罪臣前因言事獲譴，蒙我先皇帝曲賜矜全，免臣以斬而死，以囚而死，以傳訊觸忌而死。

translations.literal: Your guilty servant was earlier punished for remonstrance, yet our late emperor graciously spared me, exempting me from death by decapitation, death in prison, and death from interrogation that touched taboos.
translations.idiomatic: Your guilty servant was once punished for speaking out, yet our late emperor graciously spared me, saving me from death by the blade, death in prison, and death from interrogation that touched forbidden matters.

sentences.zh: 犯三死而未死，不求生而再生，則今日罪臣未盡之餘年，皆我先皇帝數年前所賜也。

translations.literal: Having incurred three deaths yet not dying, and not seeking life yet living again, the remaining years of your guilty servant today were all granted years ago by our late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Having faced three deaths yet not died, and not seeking life yet living still, whatever years remain to your guilty servant today were granted years ago by our late emperor.

sentences.zh: 欽奉兩宮皇太后懿旨，以醇親王之子承繼文宗顯皇帝為子，入承大統為嗣皇帝，俟嗣皇帝生有皇子，即承繼大行皇帝為嗣。

translations.literal: Reverently obeying the august edicts of the two empress dowagers, the son of Prince Chun was adopted as son to Emperor Wenzong the Manifest, entered to receive the great succession as heir emperor, and when the heir emperor should bear a son, that son would succeed the late emperor as heir.
translations.idiomatic: In reverent obedience to the august edicts of the two empress dowagers, the son of Prince Chun was adopted as son to Emperor Wenzong, ascended to receive the great succession as heir emperor, and when the heir emperor should father a son, that son would in turn succeed the late emperor as heir.

sentences.zh: 我皇上仁孝性成，承我兩宮皇太后授以寶位，將來千秋萬歲時，必能以我兩宮皇太后今日之心為心。

translations.literal: Our emperor is by nature filial and benevolent; receiving from our two empress dowagers the imperial seal, in ages to come he will surely take our two empress dowagers' hearts today as his own heart.
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor is filial and benevolent by nature; having received the imperial seal from our two empress dowagers, in the ages to come he will surely hold in his heart what they hold in theirs today.

sentences.zh: 而在廷之忠佞不齊，即眾論之異同不一。

translations.literal: Yet at court loyal and treacherous are not alike, and public opinion is not of one mind.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at court the loyal and the treacherous are not of one kind, and public opinion is likewise divided.

sentences.zh: 以宋初宰相趙普之賢，而猶首背杜太后；

translations.literal: For all the worth of Zhao Pu, chief minister at the beginning of Song, he was still the first to go against Empress Dowager Du;
translations.idiomatic: For all the worth of Zhao Pu, chief minister at the founding of the Song, he was still the first to turn against Empress Dowager Du;

sentences.zh: 以明大學士王直之為舊臣，而猶以黃𤥠請立景帝太子一疏不出我輩為愧。

translations.literal: For all that Wang Zhi was a Grand Secretary and old minister of Ming, he still felt shame that he had not submitted, as Huang Qi did, the memorial asking to establish the heir of Emperor Jing.
translations.idiomatic: For all that Wang Zhi was a Grand Secretary and veteran minister of the Ming, men still felt ashamed that none of us had submitted, as Huang Qi did, the memorial asking to establish the heir of Emperor Jing.

sentences.zh: 賢者如此，遑問不肖？

translations.literal: If the worthy are thus, how much more the unworthy?
translations.idiomatic: If even the worthy acted thus, what may be expected of the unworthy?

sentences.zh: 舊人如此，奚責新進？

translations.literal: If old ministers are thus, how can new entrants be blamed?
translations.idiomatic: If veteran ministers acted thus, how can newcomers be blamed?

sentences.zh: 名位已定者如此，況在未定。

translations.literal: If those whose titles and positions were already fixed were thus, how much more when they are not yet fixed.
translations.idiomatic: If even those whose titles and positions were already settled behaved thus, how much more when they are not yet settled.

sentences.zh: 惟有仰求我兩宮皇太后再降諭旨，將來大統，仍歸大行皇帝嗣子，嗣皇帝雖百斯男，中外臣工均不得以異言進。

translations.literal: I can only humbly beg our two empress dowagers to issue another edict: that hereafter the great succession still return to a son of the late emperor, and that though the heir emperor should have a hundred sons, ministers within and without may not advance dissenting views.
translations.idiomatic: I can only humbly beg our two empress dowagers to issue another edict declaring that hereafter the great succession shall still pass to a son of the late emperor, and that even if the heir emperor should father a hundred sons, no minister at court or in the provinces may advance a dissenting word.

sentences.zh: 如此，則猶是本朝子以傳子之家法，而我大行皇帝未有子而有子，即我兩宮皇太后未有孫而有孫，異日繩繩揖揖相引於萬代者，皆我兩宮皇太后所自出而不可移易者也。

translations.literal: Thus it would still be this dynasty's household law of son passing to son; our late emperor, though without a son, would have a son; our two empress dowagers, though without a grandson, would have a grandson; and in future ages the line stretching on in ordered succession through ten thousand generations would all spring from our two empress dowagers and could not be altered.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the dynasty would still follow its household law of father passing the throne to son: our late emperor, though without a son, would have a son; our two empress dowagers, though without a grandson, would have a grandson; and the line that in ages to come would stretch on in ordered succession through ten thousand generations would all spring from our two empress dowagers and could not be altered.

sentences.zh: 彼時罪臣即欲有言，繼思降調不得越職言事。

translations.literal: At that time your guilty servant wished to speak, but then reflected that after demotion one may not speak out of office.
translations.idiomatic: At that time your guilty servant wished to speak out, but then reflected that after demotion one may not remonstrate beyond one's rank.

sentences.zh: 今逢我大行皇帝奉安山陵，恐積久漸忘，則罪臣昔日所留以有待者，今則迫不及待矣。

translations.literal: Now, as our late emperor is laid to rest in the imperial tomb, I fear that with time this will be forgotten; what your guilty servant once reserved and waited for can no longer wait.
translations.idiomatic: Now, as our late emperor is laid to rest in the imperial tomb, I fear that with time this matter will be forgotten; what your guilty servant once held back and waited to say can no longer wait.

sentences.zh: 謹以我先皇帝所賜餘年，為我先皇帝上乞數行懿旨，惟望我兩宮皇太后、我皇上憐其哀鳴，勿以為無疾呻吟、不祥舉動，則罪臣雖死無憾。

translations.literal: Respectfully, with the remaining years our late emperor granted, I beg on behalf of our late emperor for a few lines of august edict; I only hope our two empress dowagers and our emperor will pity this mournful cry and not take it for feigned illness and groaning or an ill-omened act; then your guilty servant, though he die, will have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully, with the years our late emperor granted me, I beg on his behalf for a few lines of august edict; I only pray that our two empress dowagers and our emperor will pity this desperate cry and not dismiss it as groaning without sickness or an ill-omened act; then your guilty servant, though he die, will die without regret.

sentences.zh: 尤原我兩宮皇太后、我皇上體聖祖、世宗之心，調劑寬猛，養忠厚和平之福，任用老成；

translations.literal: I further pray our two empress dowagers and our emperor will take to heart the minds of the Kangxi and Yongzheng emperors, balance severity and leniency, nurture the blessing of honest generosity and peace, and employ seasoned men;
translations.idiomatic: I further pray that our two empress dowagers and our emperor will take to heart the spirit of the Kangxi and Yongzheng emperors, balance severity and leniency, nurture the blessing of honest generosity and peace, and employ seasoned statesmen;

sentences.zh: 毋爭外國之所獨爭，為中華留不盡；

translations.literal: do not contend for what foreign states alone contend for, and leave inexhaustible reserves for China;
translations.idiomatic: do not contest what foreign powers alone contest over, and leave inexhaustible reserves for China;

sentences.zh: 毋創祖宗之所未創，為子孫留有餘。

translations.literal: do not create what our ancestors never created, and leave surplus for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: do not innovate what our ancestors never innovated, and leave a margin for posterity.

sentences.zh: 罪臣言畢於斯，命畢於斯，謹以大統所繫上聞。

translations.literal: Your guilty servant's words end here, his life ends here; respectfully he reports what concerns the great succession.
translations.idiomatic: Your guilty servant's words end here, and his life ends here; respectfully he reports what bears on the great succession.

sentences.zh: 」吏部奏諸朝，詔憫其忠，予優恤。

translations.literal: " The Ministry of Personnel reported to the whole court; an edict pitied his loyalty and granted generous posthumous favor.
translations.idiomatic: " The Ministry of Personnel reported the matter to court; an edict commended his loyalty and granted generous posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 下群臣議，遂定以繼德宗之統為穆宗之子，無異論。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the ministers for discussion, and it was settled that he who succeeded Dezong's line should be regarded as Muzong's son, without dissent.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the ministers for discussion, and it was settled without dissent that the one who inherited Dezong's line should be regarded as Muzong's son.

sentences.zh: 可讀臨歿遺書與其子之桓，謂出薊州一步即非死所。

translations.literal: Kedu's final letter to his son Zhihuan said that one step beyond Jizhou would not be the place to die.
translations.idiomatic: In his final letter to his son Zhihuan, Kedu wrote that to take even one step beyond Jizhou would be to die in the wrong place.

sentences.zh: 之桓遂成其遺志，葬薊州。

translations.literal: Zhihuan then fulfilled his last wish and buried him at Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhihuan carried out his father's last wish and buried him at Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 都人即所居城南舊宅祠祀之。

translations.literal: The people of the capital enshrined him at his old residence south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the capital set up a shrine to him at his old residence south of the city.

sentences.zh: 有潘敦儼者，字清畏，籍江寧，總督鐸子。

translations.literal: There was Pan Dunyi, styled Qingwei, registered in Jiangning, son of Governor-General Duo.
translations.idiomatic: There was Pan Dunyi, whose courtesy name was Qingwei, registered in Jiangning and son of Governor-General Duo.

sentences.zh: 以任子官工部郎中，遷御史。

translations.literal: By privilege as an official's son he served as director in the Ministry of Works, then was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: Through the privilege granted officials' sons he became a director in the Ministry of Works and was later transferred to censor.

sentences.zh: 默念穆宗嗣統未有定議，孝哲毅皇后又仰藥殉，遂疏請表揚穆後潛德，更諡號，並解醇親王奕枻職任，詔嚴斥奪職。

translations.literal: Brooding that Muzong's succession was still unsettled and that Empress Xiaozheyi had taken poison and died in martyrdom, he memorialized to praise the late empress's hidden virtue, change her posthumous title, and remove Prince Chun Yixuan from office; an edict sternly rebuked him and stripped him of his post.
translations.idiomatic: Brooding over the unsettled question of Muzong's succession and over Empress Xiaozheyi, who had taken poison and died in martyrdom, he memorialized asking that the late empress's hidden virtues be publicly praised, her posthumous title revised, and Prince Chun Yixuan removed from office; an edict sternly rebuked him and stripped him of his post.

sentences.zh: 歸隱於酒，閱二十餘年，卒。

translations.literal: He returned home and hid himself in drink; after more than twenty years he died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired and took refuge in drink; more than twenty years later he died.

sentences.zh: 朱一新，字蓉生，浙江義烏人。

translations.literal: Zhu Yixin, styled Rongsheng, was a native of Yiwu in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yixin, whose courtesy name was Rongsheng, came from Yiwu in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 鄉舉對策語觸時忌，主司李文田特拔之。

translations.literal: In the provincial examination his policy essay touched current taboos; chief examiner Li Wentian specially advanced him.
translations.idiomatic: In the provincial examination his policy essay touched on matters then considered sensitive; chief examiner Li Wentian singled him out for special advancement.

sentences.zh: 入貲為內閣中書。

translations.literal: He purchased office as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He purchased appointment as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1876 he became a metropolitan graduate, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 法越事起，數上書主戰，又嘗畫海防策，語至切要。

translations.literal: When the Franco-Vietnamese conflict arose, he repeatedly memorialized urging war; he also once drafted a coastal defense plan, its language most urgent and essential.
translations.idiomatic: When the Franco-Vietnamese conflict broke out, he repeatedly memorialized in favor of war; he also once drafted a coastal defense plan whose language was urgent and to the point.

sentences.zh: 典湖北鄉試，稱得士。

translations.literal: He presided over the Hubei provincial examination and was praised for selecting worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: As chief examiner for the Hubei provincial examination, he was praised for having chosen worthy candidates.

sentences.zh: 十一年，轉御史，連上封事，言論侃侃，不避貴戚。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he became a censor, submitting memorial after memorial in forthright speech, not shunning powerful kin.
translations.idiomatic: In 1885 he was transferred to censor and submitted memorial after memorial in forthright language, not shrinking from powerful families.

sentences.zh: 內侍李蓮英漸著聲勢。

translations.literal: The palace eunuch Li Lianying gradually grew conspicuous in power.
translations.idiomatic: The palace eunuch Li Lianying gradually became a conspicuous figure of power.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，醇親王奕枻閱海軍，蓮英從，一新憂之。

translations.literal: The next year Prince Chun Yixuan inspected the navy and Lianying accompanied him; Yixin was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Prince Chun Yixuan inspected the navy with Lianying in attendance, and Yixin was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 而適值山東患河，燕、晉、蜀、閩患水，遂以遇災修省為言，略曰：「我朝家法，嚴馭宦寺。

translations.literal: It happened that Shandong suffered from the Yellow River, and Yan, Jin, Shu, and Min from floods; he therefore spoke under the pretext of encountering disaster and cultivating self-examination, saying in summary: "Our dynasty's household law strictly controls eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Shandong was afflicted by the Yellow River and Yan, Jin, Shu, and Min by floods; he therefore framed his remonstrance as self-examination in the face of disaster, writing in summary: "Our dynasty's household law strictly restrains eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 世祖宮中立鐵牌，更億萬年，昭為法守。

translations.literal: The Shizu emperor set up an iron tablet in the palace to stand for ten thousand ages as a proclaimed law to be kept.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu set up an iron tablet in the palace to stand for ten thousand ages as a proclaimed law never to be violated.

sentences.zh: 聖母垂簾，安得海假採辦出京，立寘重典。

translations.literal: When the holy mother held the curtain, how could An Dehai borrow procurement to leave the capital? He was immediately punished by severe statute.
translations.idiomatic: When the holy mother held court from behind the curtain, how could An Dehai use procurement as a pretext to leave the capital? He was immediately punished under the severest statute.

sentences.zh: 皇上登極，張得喜等情罪尤重，謫配為奴。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, Zhang Dexi and others, whose circumstances and crimes were still heavier, were banished and assigned as slaves.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ascended the throne, Zhang Dexi and others, whose offenses were still graver, were banished and assigned as slaves.

sentences.zh: 是以綱紀肅然，罔敢恣肆。

translations.literal: Thus discipline was stern and none dared act wantonly.
translations.idiomatic: Thus discipline was stern and none dared abuse their power.

sentences.zh: 乃今夏巡閱海軍之役，太監李蓮英隨至天津，道路譁傳，士庶駴愕，意深宮或別有不得已苦衷，匪外廷所能喻。

translations.literal: Yet in this summer's naval inspection, the eunuch Li Lianying followed to Tianjin; the roads buzzed with rumor and gentry and commoners were startled, thinking the inner palace might have some unavoidable bitter reason that the outer court could not comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: Yet during this summer's naval inspection the eunuch Li Lianying followed Prince Chun to Tianjin; rumor spread along the roads and officials and commoners alike were shocked, supposing the inner palace might have some unavoidable reason that the outer court could not fathom.

sentences.zh: 然宗籓至戚，閱軍大典，而令刑餘之輩《廣則》乎其間，其將何以詰戎兵崇體制？

translations.literal: Yet for a kinsman of the imperial clan, at a grand ceremony of inspecting the army, to let mutilated persons parade among them—how will one discipline the troops and exalt institutional dignity?
translations.idiomatic: Yet for a prince of the blood, at a grand ceremony of inspecting the army, to let castrated attendants parade in their midst—how can the troops be disciplined and institutional dignity upheld?

sentences.zh: 況作法於涼，其弊猶貪。

translations.literal: Moreover, if one makes law in leniency, its abuse will still be greed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as the saying goes, if one makes law in leniency, the abuse that follows will still be greed.

sentences.zh: 唐之監軍，豈其本意，積漸者然也。

translations.literal: Tang dynasty army supervisors—was that their original intent? It came about through gradual accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang practice of eunuch army supervisors was surely not the original intent; such things arise through gradual drift.

sentences.zh: 聖朝法制修明，萬無慮此。

translations.literal: Our holy dynasty's laws and institutions are well ordered; there is no need to fear this at all.
translations.idiomatic: Our holy dynasty's laws and institutions are well ordered; there is no need whatsoever to fear this.

sentences.zh: 而涓涓弗塞，流弊難言，杜漸防微，亦宜垂意。

translations.literal: Yet if the trickle is not stopped, flowing abuses are hard to describe; to check the gradual and guard against the minute, one should also give heed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if the trickle is not stopped, the flood of abuse is hard to describe; to halt decline at its first signs, Your Majesty should also take heed.

sentences.zh: 從古閹宦，巧於逢迎而昧於大義，引援黨類，播弄語言，使宮闈之內，疑貳漸生，而彼得售其小忠小信之為，以陰竊夫作福作威之柄。

translations.literal: Eunuchs from antiquity are skilled at flattery yet blind to great principle; they draw in factions, manipulate words, and cause doubt and division gradually to arise within the palace quarters, while they sell their petty loyalty and petty trust to secretly seize the power to bestow blessings and wield authority.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs from antiquity onward have been skilled at flattery yet blind to great principle; they draw in factions, manipulate rumor, and gradually breed suspicion within the palace, while they trade on petty shows of loyalty to secretly seize the power to reward and punish.

sentences.zh: 我皇太后、皇上明目達聰，豈有跬步之地而或敢售其欺？

translations.literal: Our empress dowager and emperor are clear-sighted and penetrating in hearing—would there be even a foot's breadth where one dared sell deception?
translations.idiomatic: Our empress dowager and emperor are clear-sighted and penetrating in judgment—would there be even a foot's breadth of ground where anyone dared peddle deception?

sentences.zh: 顧事每忽於細微，情易溺於近習，侍御僕從，罔非正人，辨之宜早辨也。

translations.literal: Yet affairs are often neglected in minute matters, and feeling easily drowns in those near at hand; attendants and servants are none but upright men—one should distinguish early.
translations.idiomatic: Yet affairs are often neglected in small matters, and affection easily drowns in those close at hand; attendants and servants are not all upright men, and they should be distinguished early.

sentences.zh: 」疏上，太后怒，詰責疏言「苦衷」何指？

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, the empress dowager was angry and demanded what the memorial meant by "bitter reason."
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, the empress dowager was furious and demanded to know what he meant by "unavoidable reason."

sentences.zh: 一新曰：「臣所謂'不得已苦衷'者，意以親籓遠涉，內侍隨行，藉以示體恤、昭慎重也。

translations.literal: Yixin said: "What your servant meant by 'unavoidable bitter reason' was that a kinsman-prince traveled far and a palace attendant accompanied him, thereby to show consideration and proclaim caution.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin replied: "What your servant meant by 'unavoidable reason' was that when a prince of the blood travels far and a palace attendant accompanies him, it is meant to show consideration and proclaim caution.

sentences.zh: 顧在朝廷為曲體，在臣庶則為創見。

translations.literal: Yet at court this is bending to show favor; among officials and commoners it is an unprecedented sight.
translations.idiomatic: At court this may count as thoughtful accommodation, but to officials and commoners it is an unprecedented sight.

sentences.zh: 風聞北洋大臣以座船迎醇親王，王弗受，而太監隨乘之，至駴人觀聽。

translations.literal: It is rumored that the Beiyang minister welcomed Prince Chun with a seat-boat; the prince did not accept, but the eunuch rode in it, to the shock of all who saw and heard.
translations.idiomatic: It is rumored that the Beiyang minister offered Prince Chun a seat on his flagship; the prince declined, but the eunuch boarded it anyway, to the astonishment of all who witnessed it.

sentences.zh: 一不謹慎，流弊遂已至斯，臣所為不能已於言也。

translations.literal: With one lapse of caution, flowing abuses have already reached this point; that is why your servant could not restrain his words.
translations.idiomatic: With a single lapse of caution, abuse has already reached this point; that is why your servant could not hold his tongue.

sentences.zh: 」詔切責，降主事。

translations.literal: " An edict sharply rebuked him and demoted him to secretary.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict sharply rebuked him and demoted him to the rank of secretary.

sentences.zh: 乞終養歸。

translations.literal: He begged to return home for lifelong mourning care.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to retire home and care for his parents for life.

sentences.zh: 張之洞督粵，建廣雅書院，延為主講。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhidong, as governor of Guangdong, built Guangya Academy and invited him as chief lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhidong governed Guangdong he founded Guangya Academy and invited Yixin to serve as its head lecturer.

sentences.zh: 一新博極群書，洞知兩漢及宋、明諸儒家法，務通經以致用。

translations.literal: Yixin was broadly learned in all books and thoroughly understood the scholarly methods of the Two Han and Song and Ming, striving to master the classics for practical use.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin was broadly learned and thoroughly understood the scholarly methods of the Han, Song, and Ming periods, striving to master the classics for practical application.

sentences.zh: 諸生有聰穎尚新奇者，必導而返諸篤實正大，語具所箸無邪堂答問中。

translations.literal: Students who were clever and fond of novelty he always guided back to solid seriousness and rectitude; his words are fully set forth in his Wuxietang Responses.
translations.idiomatic: Students who were clever and fond of novelty he always guided back toward solid seriousness and rectitude; his teaching is fully recorded in his Wuxietang Responses.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十有九。

translations.literal: He died at the age of forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 屠仁守，字梅君，湖北孝感人。

translations.literal: Tu Renshou, styled Meijun, was a native of Xiaogan in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Renshou, whose courtesy name was Meijun, came from Xiaogan in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 同治十三年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the thirteenth year of Tongzhi, he was selected as Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He became a metropolitan graduate in 1874, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，轉御史。

translations.literal: During Guangxu he became a censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangxu reign he was transferred to censor.

sentences.zh: 時政出多門，仁守因天變請修政治，條上六事，曰：杜諉卸，開壅蔽，慎動作，抑近習，軫民瘼，重國計，而歸本於大公至正、敬天勤民，疏上不省。

translations.literal: At the time policy issued from many gates; Renshou, citing heavenly warnings, asked to reform government and listed six items: stop evasion and shirking, open what is blocked, be cautious in action, restrain those near at hand, pity the people's afflictions, and weight national accounts—returning in the end to great impartiality and rectitude and revering Heaven and laboring for the people; the memorial was submitted and ignored.
translations.idiomatic: At the time policy issued from many hands; citing heavenly warnings, Renshou asked that government be reformed and listed six measures: stop evasion and shirking, open what is blocked, be cautious in action, restrain favorites at court, pity the people's afflictions, and give weight to national finance—all rooted in great impartiality and in revering Heaven and laboring for the people; the memorial went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 又以海軍報效，雜進無次，僥倖日多。

translations.literal: He also spoke because naval contributions led to disorderly advancement without rank and daily increase of undeserved favor.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized because contributions to the navy led to disorderly promotions without regard to rank and to a daily increase in undeserved favor.

sentences.zh: 仁守痛陳五弊：資敘不計，弊一；

translations.literal: Renshou painfully set forth five abuses: qualifications and seniority disregarded—abuse one;
translations.idiomatic: Renshou laid out five abuses in strong terms: qualifications and seniority disregarded—the first abuse;

sentences.zh: 名器冒濫，弊二；

translations.literal: titles and offices rashly abused—abuse two;
translations.idiomatic: titles and offices rashly abused—the second abuse;

sentences.zh: 勸懲倒置，弊三；

translations.literal: reward and punishment inverted—abuse three;
translations.idiomatic: reward and punishment inverted—the third abuse;

sentences.zh: 求益得損，財計轉虧，弊四；

translations.literal: seeking gain yet receiving loss, finances turning to deficit—abuse four;
translations.idiomatic: seeking gain yet receiving loss, state finances turning to deficit—the fourth abuse;

sentences.zh: 駔儈朋侵，莫可究詰，弊五。

translations.literal: brokers and cliques encroaching, beyond investigation—abuse five.
translations.idiomatic: brokers and cliques encroaching beyond investigation—the fifth abuse.

sentences.zh: 五弊既滋，乃生三患：患病民，患妨賢，患隳紀綱法度。

translations.literal: When the five abuses flourished, three perils arose: peril to the afflicted people, peril of obstructing the worthy, peril of destroying discipline and law.
translations.idiomatic: As these five abuses flourished, three perils arose: peril to the suffering people, peril of obstructing the worthy, and peril of destroying discipline and law.

sentences.zh: 「特以自海軍衙門達之，奉懿旨行之，毋或敢貿然入告，遂使謗騰衢路，而朝廷不聞，患伏隱微，而朝廷不知，群小得志，寵賂滋張。

translations.literal: " Because it came down from the Naval Office and was carried out by august edict, none dared rashly report in, so slander filled the streets yet the court did not hear; perils lay hidden in minute places yet the court did not know; petty men got their way and favor and bribes spread.
translations.idiomatic: " Because the matter came down from the Naval Office and was carried out by august edict, none dared rashly report it, so slander filled the streets while the court heard nothing; dangers lay hidden in small matters while the court knew nothing; petty men had their way and favor and bribes spread unchecked.

sentences.zh: 若不停止，即承平無事，猶或召亂，況時局孔艱乎？

translations.literal: If this is not stopped, even in untroubled peace disorder may be summoned—how much more when the times are greatly hard?
translations.idiomatic: If this is not stopped, even in untroubled times disorder may be summoned—how much more when the situation is so dire?

sentences.zh: 」疏入，詔從之，權貴益側目。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, an edict followed it, and the powerful grew still more hostile.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, an edict approved his recommendations, and the powerful grew still more hostile toward him.

sentences.zh: 十五年，太后歸政，仁守慮僉人讒構兩宮，易生嫌隙，疏請依高宗訓政往事：「凡部院題本、尋常奏事，如常例；

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the empress dowager returned power; Renshou feared that petty men would slander and set the two palaces against each other, easily breeding suspicion, and memorialized asking to follow the precedent of the Gaozong emperor's regency instruction: "All routine memorials from ministries and boards and ordinary reports shall follow usual practice;
translations.idiomatic: In 1889, when the empress dowager returned power to the throne, Renshou feared that petty men would sow discord between the two palaces and breed suspicion; he memorialized asking that the precedent of Emperor Gaozong's regency instruction be followed: "All routine memorials from ministries and boards and ordinary reports shall follow usual practice;

sentences.zh: 外省密摺、廷臣封奏，仍書皇太后、皇上聖鑒，俟慈覽後施行。

translations.literal: secret memorials from the provinces and sealed reports from court ministers shall still be addressed for the sacred inspection of the empress dowager and emperor, and carried out only after her gracious review.
translations.idiomatic: secret memorials from the provinces and sealed reports from court ministers shall still be addressed for the sacred inspection of the empress dowager and the emperor, and carried out only after her gracious review.

sentences.zh: 」並請太后居慈寧宮，節遊觀。

translations.literal: " He also asked that the empress dowager reside at Cining Palace and moderate excursions and sightseeing.
translations.idiomatic: " He also asked that the empress dowager reside at Cining Palace and moderate her excursions and sightseeing.

sentences.zh: 詔嚴責，革職永不敘用。

translations.literal: An edict severely censured him, stripped him of office, and never again permitted his reappointment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict severely censured him, stripped him of office, and barred him from ever serving again.

sentences.zh: 既歸，主講山西令德堂。

translations.literal: After returning home, he served as chief lecturer at Lingde Hall in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home, he served as chief lecturer at Lingde Hall in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，兩宮西狩，起用五品京堂，授光祿寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when the two palaces went west on the imperial hunt, he was recalled as a fifth-rank capital official and appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900, when the court fled west, he was recalled as a fifth-rank capital official and appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon after, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 吳兆泰，字星階，籍麻城。

translations.literal: Wu Zhaotai, styled Xingjie, was registered in Macheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhaotai, styled Xingjie, was a native of Macheng.

sentences.zh: 與仁守友善，互相厲以道義。

translations.literal: He was friendly with Renshou, and they spurred each other on with moral principle.
translations.idiomatic: He was close friends with Tu Renshou, and they urged each other on in duty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年進士，閱十年，以編修考授御史。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Guangxu reign he passed the jinshi examination; after ten years, through examination as a compiler, he was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1876, and ten years later, after evaluation in his post as compiler, he was appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 時國防廢弛，海軍尤不振，朝廷乃移其費修頤和園。

translations.literal: At the time national defense was neglected, and the navy was especially weak; the court therefore diverted its funds to repair the Summer Palace.
translations.idiomatic: National defense had fallen into neglect, the navy above all was in decline, and the court diverted those funds to restore the Summer Palace.

sentences.zh: 兆泰上疏力爭，略謂：「畿輔奇災，嗷鴻遍野，僵僕載塗，此正朝廷減膳徹樂之時，非土木興作之日。

translations.literal: Zhaotai submitted a memorial arguing forcefully, in essence saying: "The capital region has suffered extraordinary calamity; starving people wail like geese across the fields, and corpses lie piled on the roads. Now is precisely the time for the court to reduce meals and withdraw music—not the day for construction projects.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaotai submitted a memorial arguing forcefully, in essence saying: "The capital region has been struck by extraordinary disaster; starving people wail across the countryside, and the dead lie heaped upon the roads. This is precisely the moment for the court to eat sparingly and suspend festivities—not to launch building projects.

sentences.zh: 乞罷園工，以慰民望，以光繼列祖列宗儉德。

translations.literal: I beg that the garden works be halted, to satisfy the people's hopes and to glorify the frugal virtue inherited from successive emperors and ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that work on the gardens be stopped, to answer the people's hopes and to honor the frugal virtue of our successive emperors and ancestors.

sentences.zh: 」太后怒，罷其官。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager was angered and dismissed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager was enraged and stripped him of his post.

sentences.zh: 歸里後，歷主龍泉、經心書院講席，充學務公所議長。

translations.literal: After returning home, he successively headed the lecture chairs at Longquan and Jingxin Academies and served as chairman of the public school affairs council.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home, he successively headed the lecture chairs at Longquan and Jingxin Academies and served as chairman of the public school affairs council.

sentences.zh: 宣統二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Xuantong reign, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1910.

sentences.zh: 其先有何金壽者，字鐵生，籍江夏。

translations.literal: Earlier there was one He Jinshou, styled Tiesheng, registered in Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier there was He Jinshou, styled Tiesheng, a native of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 同治元年一甲二名進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign he passed the jinshi examination ranked second in the first class and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he passed the jinshi examination ranked second in the first class and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 出督河南學政，還充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: He went out to supervise education in Henan; on his return he served as diarist-attendant for daily lectures on the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to serve as educational commissioner in Henan, and on his return was appointed diarist-attendant for the daily lecture on the classics.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，晉飢，上儲糧平糶策。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Guangxu reign, Shanxi suffered famine; he presented a plan for selling stored grain at fair prices.
translations.idiomatic: In 1876, when Shanxi was stricken by famine, he submitted a plan to release stored grain for sale at fair prices.

sentences.zh: 越二年，畿輔旱，金壽曰：「此樞臣可盡彈也！

translations.literal: Two years later there was drought in the capital region; Jinshou said: "The grand councilors can all be impeached for this!
translations.idiomatic: Two years later drought struck the capital region, and Jinshou said: "The grand councilors should all be impeached for this!

sentences.zh: 」乃援漢代天災策免三公為言，請罷樞臣、回天意。

translations.literal: " He then cited the Han dynasty precedent of dismissing the Three Ducal Ministers in response to heavenly calamity, asking that the grand councilors be dismissed to turn back heaven's will.
translations.idiomatic: " He then cited the Han dynasty precedent of dismissing the Three Ducal Ministers when heaven sent disaster, and asked that the grand councilors be removed to turn heaven's wrath aside.

sentences.zh: 越日，命下，恭親王奕訢等五人並褫職留任，直聲震一時。

translations.literal: The next day orders were issued: Prince Gong Yixin and four others were all stripped of office but retained in their posts, and his outspoken reputation shook the age.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the order came down: Prince Gong Yixin and four others were all stripped of rank yet kept in place, and his blunt honesty made a sensation throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 五年，复瀝陳時弊，斥言中外臣工皆瞻徇，侃侃不撓。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again submitted detailed memorials on current abuses, sternly declaring that ministers at court and in the provinces all looked to others and deferred; he spoke forthrightly without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: In 1879 he again submitted detailed memorials on the abuses of the day, denouncing ministers at court and in the provinces for looking only to their superiors and deferring to one another; he spoke plainly and would not be swayed.

sentences.zh: 上以所奏為祛積習，特宣示。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded what was memorialized as removing accumulated habits and specially promulgated it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated the memorial as a call to break entrenched habits and had it specially promulgated.

sentences.zh: 忤當軸意，出知江蘇揚州府。

translations.literal: Offending those in power, he was sent out as prefect of Yangzhou in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Having offended those in power, he was sent out to serve as prefect of Yangzhou in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 未出都，會崇厚與俄定約，敕下廷臣議。

translations.literal: Before he had left the capital, Chonghou concluded a treaty with Russia; an edict ordered court ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Before he left the capital, Chonghou concluded a treaty with Russia, and an edict ordered the court ministers to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 金壽引西國上下議院例，請資眾論，折強敵。

translations.literal: Jinshou cited the Western precedent of upper and lower parliamentary houses, asking to rely on public opinion to defeat the strong enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshou cited Western practice in the upper and lower houses of parliament, asking that public opinion be enlisted to stand up to a powerful foe.

sentences.zh: 逾歲到官，錄築堤功，賜三品服。

translations.literal: More than a year later he reached his post; his dike-building achievements were recorded and he was granted third-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he took up his post; his achievements in building dikes were recorded, and he was granted third-rank robes.

sentences.zh: 八年秋，禱雨中暍，病卒，貧不能歸葬。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the eighth year, while praying for rain he suffered heatstroke, fell ill and died; he was too poor to return home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of 1882, while praying for rain he was overcome by heat, fell ill and died, and his family was too poor to bring his body home for burial.

sentences.zh: 總督左宗棠等上其事於朝，謂有古循吏風雲。

translations.literal: Governor-General Zuo Zongtang and others reported the matter to court, saying he possessed the manner of an ancient virtuous local official.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Zuo Zongtang and others reported the matter to court, saying he had the bearing of an ancient virtuous local official.

sentences.zh: 安維峻，字曉峰，甘肅秦安人。

translations.literal: An Weijun, styled Xiaofeng, was a native of Qin'an in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: An Weijun, styled Xiaofeng, was a native of Qin'an in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 初以拔貢朝考，用七品小京官。

translations.literal: At first, through the tribute-student palace examination, he was appointed as a seventh-rank minor capital official.
translations.idiomatic: At first, after passing the palace examination as a tribute student, he was appointed a seventh-rank minor capital official.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，成進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Guangxu reign he passed the jinshi examination, became a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1880 he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 十九年，轉御史。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1893 he was transferred to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 未一年，先後上六十餘疏。

translations.literal: In less than a year he submitted more than sixty memorials in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In less than a year he submitted more than sixty memorials in succession.

sentences.zh: 日韓釁起，時上雖親政，遇事必請太后意旨，和戰不能獨決，及戰屢敗，世皆歸咎李鴻章主款。

translations.literal: When the Sino-Japanese conflict arose, although the emperor had taken power, on every matter he had to seek the empress dowager's instructions; he could not independently decide war or peace. When battles were repeatedly lost, the world blamed Li Hongzhang for advocating peace terms.
translations.idiomatic: When conflict broke out with Japan, although the emperor had taken power, he still had to seek the empress dowager's instructions on every matter and could not decide war or peace on his own. After repeated defeats, public opinion blamed Li Hongzhang for pushing peace talks.

sentences.zh: 於是維峻上言：「李鴻章平日挾外洋以自重，固不欲戰，有言戰者，動遭呵斥。

translations.literal: Thereupon Weijun memorialized: "Li Hongzhang usually relies on foreign powers to bolster himself; he naturally does not wish to fight. Whoever speaks of fighting is promptly berated.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Weijun memorialized: "Li Hongzhang habitually uses foreign backing to magnify his own authority; he plainly does not want war, and anyone who speaks of fighting is at once rebuked.

sentences.zh: 淮軍將領望風希旨，未見賊先退避，偶見賊即驚潰。

translations.literal: Huai Army generals read the wind and seek to please; before sighting the enemy they already withdraw; if they happen to see the enemy they panic and rout.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai Army generals take their cue from him and seek to please; they retreat before they even see the enemy, and if they happen to encounter the foe they panic and scatter.

sentences.zh: 我不能激勵將士，決計一戰，乃俯首聽命於賊。

translations.literal: We cannot inspire officers and soldiers and resolve on a decisive battle, yet bow our heads and obey the enemy's commands.
translations.idiomatic: We cannot rouse our officers and soldiers and commit to a decisive battle, yet we bow our heads and take orders from the enemy.

sentences.zh: 然則此舉非議和也，直納款耳，不但誤國，而且賣國。

translations.literal: Then this action is not debating peace—it is outright surrender. It not only misleads the state but sells out the country.
translations.idiomatic: In that case this is not peace talks at all, but outright surrender. It not only misleads the state—it betrays it.

sentences.zh: 中外臣民，無不切齒痛恨。

translations.literal: Officials and common people at home and abroad all gnash their teeth with hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and common people at home and abroad seethe with hatred.

sentences.zh: 而又謂和議出自皇太后，太監李蓮英實左右之，臣未敢深信。

translations.literal: Some also say the peace talks issued from the empress dowager, with the eunuch Li Lianying actually steering them; your servant dares not fully believe this.
translations.idiomatic: Some also say the peace talks came from the empress dowager herself, with the eunuch Li Lianying truly pulling the strings; your servant dares not fully believe this.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 皇太后既歸政，若仍遇事牽制，將何以上對祖宗，下對天下臣民？

translations.literal: Since the empress dowager has returned power, if she still restrains affairs at every turn, how can she face the ancestors above and the officials and people of the realm below?
translations.idiomatic: Since the empress dowager has returned power, if she still restrains affairs at every turn, how can she answer to the ancestors above or to the officials and people of the realm below?

sentences.zh: 至李蓮英是何人斯，敢干政事乎？

translations.literal: As for Li Lianying—who is he to dare meddle in state affairs?
translations.idiomatic: As for Li Lianying—who is he to dare meddle in state affairs?

sentences.zh: 如果屬實，律以祖宗法制，豈復可容？

translations.literal: If this is true, judged by ancestral laws and institutions, how could it still be tolerated?
translations.idiomatic: If this is true, judged by the laws and institutions of our ancestors, how could it be tolerated?

sentences.zh: 唯是朝廷受李鴻章哃喝，不及詳審，而樞臣中或系私黨，甘心左袒，或恐決裂，姑事調停。

translations.literal: Only, the court is cowed by Li Hongzhang's browbeating and cannot examine matters thoroughly; among the grand councilors some belong to his private faction and willingly favor him, while some fear a rupture and for now merely mediate.
translations.idiomatic: Only the court is cowed by Li Hongzhang's intimidation and cannot examine matters carefully; among the grand councilors, some belong to his private faction and willingly take his side, while others fear a rupture and for now merely mediate.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章事事挾制朝廷，抗違諭旨。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang on every matter coerces the court and resists imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: On every matter Li Hongzhang coerces the court and defies imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 唯冀皇上赫然震怒，明正其罪，佈告天下，如是而將士有不奮興、賊人有不破滅者，即請斬臣以正妄言之罪。

translations.literal: I only hope Your Majesty will suddenly blaze with anger, clearly establish his crimes, and proclaim them to all under heaven. If after this officers and soldiers do not rouse themselves and the enemy is not destroyed, then I beg to be executed to atone for the crime of reckless speech.
translations.idiomatic: I only hope Your Majesty will blaze with righteous anger, clearly establish his crimes, and proclaim them to all under heaven. If after that the officers and soldiers do not rouse themselves and the enemy is not destroyed, then I beg to be executed to atone for reckless speech.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，上諭：「軍國要事，仰承懿訓遵行，天下共諒。

translations.literal: " When the memorial arrived, the emperor instructed: "Important military and state affairs are carried out deferring to Her Majesty's gracious instruction; all under heaven understand this together.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial arrived, the emperor instructed: "Important military and state affairs are carried out in accordance with Her Majesty's gracious instruction; all under heaven understand this.

sentences.zh: 乃安維峻封奏，託諸傳聞，竟有'皇太后遇事牽制'之語，妄言無忌，恐開離間之端。

translations.literal: Yet An Weijun's sealed memorial relies on hearsay and actually contains the words 'the empress dowager restrains affairs at every turn'—reckless speech without restraint, fearing it may open a breach of discord.
translations.idiomatic: Yet An Weijun's sealed memorial rests on hearsay and actually contains the words 'the empress dowager restrains affairs at every turn'—reckless speech without restraint that may open a breach of discord.

sentences.zh: 」命革職發軍台。

translations.literal: " He was ordered stripped of office and sent to serve at a military post.
translations.idiomatic: " He was stripped of office and exiled to serve at a frontier military post.

sentences.zh: 維峻以言獲罪，直聲震中外，人多榮之。

translations.literal: Wei Jun was punished because of his words; his upright voice shook within and without; many people honored him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jun was punished for speaking out, yet his forthright voice resounded across the realm, and many regarded it as an honor to stand with him.

sentences.zh: 訪問者萃於門，餞送者塞於道，或贈以言，或資以贐，車馬飲食，眾皆為供應。

translations.literal: Those who came to visit gathered at his gate; those who came to send him off filled the road; some gave words, some supplied parting gifts; carriages, horses, food, and drink—all were provided by the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Visitors thronged his gate, and well-wishers lined the road to see him off; some offered words of encouragement, others parting gifts, while the crowd supplied horses, carriages, food, and drink.

sentences.zh: 抵戍所，都統以下皆敬以客禮，聘主講掄才書院。

translations.literal: When he reached the place of exile, everyone from the commander down treated him with guest courtesy and engaged him as principal lecturer at the Lun Cai Academy.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his place of exile, the commander and all ranks below received him with the courtesy due a guest and appointed him principal lecturer at the Lun Cai Academy.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，釋還，遂歸里。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, he was released and returned, and then went home.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was released from exile and returned home.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，起授內閣侍讀，充京師大學總教習。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, he was recalled and appointed Reader of the Grand Secretariat, and served as Chief Instructor of the Capital University.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he was recalled to office, appointed Reader of the Grand Secretariat, and made Chief Instructor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，复辭歸。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong, he again resigned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Xuantong reign he resigned once more and went home.

sentences.zh: 越十有五年，卒。

translations.literal: After fifteen more years, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen years later he died.

sentences.zh: 維峻崇樸實，尚​​踐履，不喜為博辨，尤嚴義利之分。

translations.literal: Wei Jun honored plainness and substance, valued practical conduct, disliked wide disputation, and was especially strict about the distinction between righteousness and profit.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jun prized plain honesty and practical conduct, had little taste for clever debate, and was especially rigorous in separating righteousness from profit.

sentences.zh: 歸後退隱柏崖，杜門著書，隱然以名教綱常為己任。

translations.literal: After returning, he retired to Baiya, shut his doors, and wrote books, tacitly taking the norms of teaching and moral principle as his own responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: After his return he withdrew to Baiya, closed his doors to the world, and wrote at his desk, quietly taking the preservation of Confucian moral order as his personal duty.

sentences.zh: 每談及世變，輒憂形於色，卒抑鬱以終。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke of the changes in the age, distress would appear on his face; in the end he died in depression.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke of the turmoil of the times, grief showed plainly on his face, and he died at last in despondency.

sentences.zh: 著有四書講義、詩文集。

translations.literal: He authored Commentaries on the Four Books and a collection of poetry and prose.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Commentaries on the Four Books and a collected volume of poetry and prose.

sentences.zh: 文悌，字仲恭，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Wen Ti, courtesy name Zhonggong, of the Guwalgiya clan, a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Ti, styled Zhonggong, was a Manchu of the Guwalgiya clan and the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 以筆帖式歷戶部郎中，出為河南知府，改御史。

translations.literal: Starting as a clerk, he rose through the Ministry of Revenue to department director, was posted out as prefect of Henan, and was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: Beginning as a clerk, he served in the Ministry of Revenue until he reached the rank of department director, was appointed prefect of Henan, and was later transferred to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十四年，變法詔下，禮部主事王照應詔上言，尚書許應騤不為代奏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu, when the reform edict was issued, Wang Zhao, a section chief in the Ministry of Rites, submitted a memorial in response to the imperial call, but Minister Xu Yingkui would not forward it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu, when the reform edict was promulgated, Wang Zhao of the Ministry of Rites answered the imperial summons with a memorial, but Minister Xu Yingkui refused to transmit it.

sentences.zh: 御史宋伯魯、楊深秀聯名劾以守舊迂謬，阻撓新政，諭應騤明白回奏，覆奏稱珍惜名器，物色通才，並辭連工部主事康有為，請罷斥驅逐。

translations.literal: Censors Song Bolu and Yang Shenxiu jointly impeached him for clinging to the old ways, obstinacy, and obstructing the new policies. Xu was ordered to reply clearly; in his reply he said he cherished official appointments and sought capable men, but also implicated Kang Youwei, section chief in the Ministry of Works, and asked that he be dismissed and expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Song Bolu and Yang Shenxiu jointly memorialized accusing him of hidebound conservatism and obstruction of the new policies. Xu was ordered to reply in explicit terms; he answered that he valued official appointments and sought talented men, but also named Kang Youwei of the Ministry of Works and asked that he be dismissed and driven out.

sentences.zh: 奏上，以抑格言路，首違詔旨，禮部尚書、侍郎皆革職，賞照四品京堂。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, for suppressing free speech and being the first to violate the edict's intent, the Minister and Vice Ministers of Rites were all dismissed, and Wang Zhao was rewarded with a fourth-rank capital office.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the Minister and Vice Ministers of Rites were dismissed for suppressing remonstrance and being the first to defy the reform edict, while Wang Zhao was rewarded with a fourth-rank capital appointment.

sentences.zh: 文悌以言官為人指使，黨庇報復，紊亂臺諫，遂上疏言：「康有為向不相識，忽踵門求謁，送以所著書籍，閱其著作，以變法為宗。

translations.literal: Wen Ti believed that censors were being directed by others, shielding factions and seeking revenge and throwing the censorate into disorder, so he submitted a memorial stating: "I had never known Kang Youwei before; suddenly he came to my door seeking an audience and presented me with his writings. Reading his works, I found he takes reform as his core doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Ti held that censors were being manipulated by others, shielding factions and settling scores and thereby throwing the censorate into disorder, and so he submitted a memorial saying: "I had never known Kang Youwei before; suddenly he came to my door seeking an audience and gave me his writings. Reading them, I found that he makes reform his central doctrine.

sentences.zh: 而尤堪駭詫者，託辭孔子改制，謂孔子作春秋西狩獲麟為受命之符，以春秋變週為孔子當一代王者。

translations.literal: What is especially shocking is that, invoking Confucius's doctrine of institutional change, he claims that when Confucius wrote the Spring and Autumn Annals, the capture of the qilin during the western hunt was a sign of receiving Heaven's mandate, and that through the Spring and Autumn Annals Confucius transformed Zhou and thus was acting as the sage-king of his age.
translations.idiomatic: What is most shocking is that, under the pretext of Confucius's doctrine of institutional reform, he claims that when Confucius wrote the Spring and Autumn Annals, the capture of the qilin on the western hunt was a token of receiving Heaven's mandate—that through the Annals Confucius transformed Zhou and was in effect the sage-king of his generation.

sentences.zh: 明似推崇孔子，實則自申其改制之義。

translations.literal: Outwardly he seems to exalt Confucius, but in fact he is advancing his own theory of institutional reform.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he appears to honor Confucius, but in truth he is promoting his own doctrine of institutional change.

sentences.zh: 乃知康有為之學術，正如漢書嚴助所謂以春秋為蘇秦縱橫者耳。

translations.literal: Thus one sees that Kang Youwei's learning is just what Yan Zhu in the Book of Han called using the Spring and Autumn Annals as a cover for Su Qin's brand of factional scheming.
translations.idiomatic: From this one can see that Kang Youwei's scholarship is precisely what Yan Zhu in the Book of Han described as wielding the Spring and Autumn Annals in the manner of Su Qin's factional intrigue.

sentences.zh: 及聆其談治術，則專主西學，以師法日本為良策。

translations.literal: When I listened to him discuss methods of governance, he advocated Western learning exclusively and held that following Japan's example was the best policy.
translations.idiomatic: When I heard him speak on methods of governance, he advocated Western learning alone and held that taking Japan as a model was the best course.

sentences.zh: 如近來時務、知新等報所論，尊俠力，伸民權，興黨會，改制度，甚則欲去拜跪之禮儀，廢滿、漢之文字，平君臣之尊卑，改男女之外內。

translations.literal: As the recent Shiwu, Zhixin, and other newspapers discuss: exalting martial prowess, expanding people's rights, establishing political clubs, changing institutions—even to the point of wishing to abolish bowing and kneeling rituals, discard Manchu and Chinese writing, level the hierarchy between sovereign and subject, and alter the separation of men and women indoors and out.
translations.idiomatic: As recent papers such as Shiwu and Zhixin argue, they exalt martial force, expand popular rights, establish political clubs, and change institutions—going so far as to wish away bowing and kneeling, abolish both Manchu and Chinese script, erase the distinction between sovereign and subject, and overturn the separation of men and women within and without the home.

sentences.zh: 直似只須中國一變而為外洋政教風俗，即可立致富強，而不知其勢小則群起鬥爭，立可召亂；

translations.literal: It is as if China need only transform at once into foreign polities, teachings, and customs to become instantly wealthy and strong, without realizing that on a small scale this would set people fighting one another and immediately invite disorder;
translations.idiomatic: It is as though China need only transform overnight into foreign polities, teachings, and customs to become instantly rich and strong—without realizing that on a small scale this would set people at one another's throats and at once summon chaos;

sentences.zh: 大則各便私利，賣國何難？

translations.literal: on a large scale each would serve private gain—what difficulty would there be in selling out the country?
translations.idiomatic: on a large scale each would serve private advantage—what difficulty would there be in selling out the country?

sentences.zh: 曾以此言戒勸康有為，乃不思省改，且更私聚數百人，在輦轂之下，立為保國會，日執途人而號之曰：'中國必亡，必亡！

translations.literal: I once used these words to warn and counsel Kang Youwei, but he gave no thought to correction; instead he secretly gathered several hundred men right under the capital and established a Society for the Preservation of the Nation, daily seizing passersby and shouting at them: 'China must perish, must perish!
translations.idiomatic: I once used these words to warn and counsel Kang Youwei, but he gave no thought to reform; instead he secretly gathered several hundred men right under the capital and established a Society for the Preservation of the Nation, daily seizing passersby and shouting at them: 'China must perish, must perish!

sentences.zh: '以致士夫惶駭，庶眾搖惑。

translations.literal: ' causing scholars to panic and the common people to waver in confusion.
translations.idiomatic: so that scholars were thrown into alarm and the common people were left unsettled.

sentences.zh: 設使四民解體，大盜生心，藉此以集聚匪徒，招誘黨羽，因而犯上作亂，未知康有為又何以善其後？

translations.literal: Suppose the four classes dissolve and great bandits take heart: using this to assemble ruffians and recruit partisans, and thereby rise in rebellion against their superiors—how does Kang Youwei propose to set matters right afterward?
translations.idiomatic: Suppose the four classes fall apart and great brigands take heart—using this to gather ruffians and recruit partisans and thereby rise in rebellion against their superiors: how does Kang Youwei propose to set matters right afterward?

sentences.zh: 曾令其將忠君愛國合為一事，勿徒欲保中國而置我大清於度外，康有為亦似悔之。

translations.literal: I once urged him to unite loyalty to the sovereign with love of country as one matter, and not merely wish to preserve China while placing our Great Qing outside consideration; Kang Youwei also seemed to regret this.
translations.idiomatic: I once urged him to make loyalty to the sovereign and love of country one and the same, and not merely wish to preserve China while setting our Great Qing aside; Kang Youwei also seemed to regret it.

sentences.zh: 又曾手書御史名單一紙，欲臣倡首鼓動眾人伏闕痛哭，力請變法。

translations.literal: He also once wrote out by hand a list of censor names, wishing me to take the lead in stirring up a crowd to prostrate themselves at the palace gate weeping and urging reform with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: He also once wrote out by hand a list of censor names, wishing me to take the lead in stirring the crowd to prostrate themselves weeping at the palace gate and urgently petition for reform.

sentences.zh: 當告以言官結黨為國朝大禁，此事萬不可為。

translations.literal: I told him that factional alliance among censors is a grave prohibition of our dynasty—such a thing must on no account be done.
translations.idiomatic: I told him that censors forming factions was a grave prohibition of our dynasty and that such a thing must on no account be done.

sentences.zh: 以康有為一人在京城任意妄為，遍結言官，把持國事，已足駭人聽聞；

translations.literal: That Kang Youwei alone in the capital should act recklessly at will, win over censors everywhere, and control state affairs is already enough to shock the ear;
translations.idiomatic: That Kang Youwei alone in the capital should act recklessly at will, win over censors everywhere, and control state affairs is already shocking enough;

sentences.zh: 而宋伯魯、楊深秀身為臺諫，公然聯名庇黨，誣參朝廷大臣，此風何可長也！

translations.literal: yet Song Bolu and Yang Shenxiu, as censors themselves, openly joined in memorializing to shield a faction and falsely accuse court ministers—how can such a trend be tolerated!
translations.idiomatic: yet Song Bolu and Yang Shenxiu, as censors themselves, openly joined in memorializing to shield a faction and falsely impeach court ministers—how can such a trend be allowed to grow!

sentences.zh: 伏思國家變法，原為整頓國事，非欲敗壞國事。

translations.literal: Respectfully considering the matter, the state's reform was originally meant to put national affairs in order, not to ruin them.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully considered, the state's reform was originally intended to put national affairs in order, not to ruin them.

sentences.zh: 譬如屋宇年久失修，自應招工依法改造，若任三五喜事之徒曳之傾倒，而曰非此不能從速，恐梁棟毀折，且將傷人。

translations.literal: It is like a house long neglected in repair: one ought to hire workers and renovate it according to proper methods. If a few reckless busybodies are allowed to drag it down, claiming nothing else can speed the work, I fear the beams and rafters will break—and people will be hurt as well.
translations.idiomatic: It is like a house long neglected: one ought to hire workers and renovate it by proper methods. If a few reckless busybodies are allowed to pull it down, claiming nothing else can speed the work, I fear the beams and rafters will collapse—and people will be hurt as well.

sentences.zh: 康有為之變法，何以異是？

translations.literal: How does Kang Youwei's reform differ from this?
translations.idiomatic: How does Kang Youwei's reform differ from this?

sentences.zh: 此所以不敢已於言也。

translations.literal: This is why I dare not hold my tongue.
translations.idiomatic: This is why I dare not hold my tongue.

sentences.zh: 」疏上，斥回原衙門行走。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, he was stripped of his post and ordered back to serve at his original yamen.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial reached the throne, he was dismissed from his post and ordered back to serve at his original department.

sentences.zh: 太后復訓政，賞文悌知府，旋授河南知府。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager resumed regency, Wen Ti was rewarded with the rank of prefect and soon appointed prefect of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager resumed regency, Wen Ti was rewarded with the rank of prefect and was soon appointed prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，兩宮西狩，文悌迎駕，擢貴西道。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when both palaces fled west, Wen Ti met the imperial retinue and was promoted to Intendant of Guixi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, when both courts fled west, Wen Ti met the imperial retinue and was promoted to Intendant of Guixi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 乞病歸，卒。

translations.literal: He requested leave due to illness and returned home, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He requested leave on grounds of illness, returned home, and died.

sentences.zh: 江春霖，字杏村，福建莆田人。

translations.literal: Jiang Chunlin, courtesy name Xingcun, a native of Putian in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Chunlin, styled Xingcun, was a native of Putian in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the twentieth year of Guangxu, he was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twentieth year of Guangxu, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，轉御史，首論都御史陸寶忠幹煙禁，不宜為台長，劾親貴及樞臣疆臣，章凡數十上。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to censor; he first memorialized that Grand Censor Lu Baozhong had interfered with the opium prohibition and was unfit to head the censorate, and impeached imperial relatives, grand councillors, and provincial governors—altogether submitting several dozen memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to censor; he first memorialized that Grand Censor Lu Baozhong had meddled in the opium prohibition and was unfit to head the censorate, and he impeached imperial relatives, grand councillors, and provincial governors—altogether submitting several dozen memorials.

sentences.zh: 德宗季葉，袁世凱出督畿輔，入贊樞廷，權勢傾一時。

translations.literal: In the late years of Emperor Dezong, Yuan Shikai went out to govern the capital region and entered the Grand Council to assist; his power and influence dominated the age.
translations.idiomatic: In the late years of Emperor Guangxu, Yuan Shikai went out to govern the capital region, entered the Grand Council to assist, and his power dominated the age.

sentences.zh: 春霖獨論列十二事，謂：「洪範有言：'臣之有作威作福，其害於爾家，兇於爾國。

translations.literal: Chunlin alone laid out twelve charges, stating: "The Hongfan says: 'When ministers practice intimidation and bestow favors, it harms your house and brings ruin to your state.
translations.idiomatic: Chunlin alone laid out twelve charges, stating: "The Hongfan says: 'When ministers practice intimidation and bestow favors, it harms your house and brings ruin to your state.

sentences.zh: '左氏傳云：'受君之祿，是以聚黨，有黨而爭命，罪孰大焉？

translations.literal: ' The Zuo Commentary says: 'One who receives the ruler's stipend thereby gathers a faction; to have a faction and contend for power—what crime could be greater?
translations.idiomatic: ' The Zuo Commentary says: 'One who receives the ruler's stipend thereby gathers a faction; to have a faction and contend for power—what crime could be greater?

sentences.zh: '今世凱所為，其心即使無他，其跡要難共諒。

translations.literal: ' As for what Shikai has done today, even if his heart harbors no other intent, his conduct is hard for others to trust.
translations.idiomatic: ' As for what Shikai has done today, even if his heart harbors no other intent, his conduct is hard for others to trust.

sentences.zh: 歷考史冊所載權臣，大者貽憂君國，小者禍及身家。

translations.literal: Examining the powerful ministers recorded in history, the grave cases brought anxiety upon ruler and state, the lesser ones brought disaster upon person and family.
translations.idiomatic: A survey of powerful ministers recorded in history shows that in the gravest cases they brought anxiety upon ruler and state, and in lesser ones disaster upon person and family.

sentences.zh: 窺竊神器之徒，姑置勿論，即功在社稷，如霍光、李德裕、張居正，亦以權寵太盛，傾覆相尋。

translations.literal: Setting aside those who usurped the sacred vessel, even men whose merit served the altars of soil and grain—such as Huo Guang, Li Deyu, and Zhang Juzheng—succumbed one after another because their power and favor grew too great.
translations.idiomatic: Setting aside those who usurped the imperial throne, even men whose merit served the altars of soil and grain—such as Huo Guang, Li Deyu, and Zhang Juzheng—fell one after another because their power and favor grew too great.

sentences.zh: 今不獨為國家計，宜加裁抑，即欲使世凱子孫長守富貴，亦不可無善處之法。

translations.literal: Now, not only for the sake of the state ought restraint be applied; even if one wished Shikai's descendants to long preserve their wealth and rank, there must be a proper way to manage matters.
translations.idiomatic: Now, not only for the sake of the state ought restraint be applied; even if one wished Shikai's descendants to long preserve their wealth and rank, there must be a proper way to manage the matter.

sentences.zh: 」嗣是糾彈世凱及慶親王奕劻父子，連上八疏，皆不報，然朝貴頗嚴憚之。

translations.literal: " Thereafter he impeached Shikai and Prince Qing Yikuang and his son, submitting eight memorials in succession, all unanswered, yet the powerful at court greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereafter he impeached Yuan Shikai and Prince Qing Yikuang and his son, submitting eight memorials in succession, all of which went unanswered, yet the powerful at court greatly feared him.

sentences.zh: 宣統改元，醇親王載灃既攝政，其弟載洵、載濤分長軍諮、海軍，頗用事。

translations.literal: When the Xuantong reign began, Prince Chun Zaifeng had become regent; his brothers Zaixun and Zaitao respectively headed the Army Advisory Council and the navy and wielded considerable power.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuantong reign began, Prince Chun Zaifeng had become regent; his brothers Zaixun and Zaitao respectively headed the Army Advisory Council and the navy and wielded considerable influence.

sentences.zh: 春霖謂：「古者鄭寵共叔，失教旋譏，漢驕厲王，不容終病，載在史冊，為萬世戒。

translations.literal: Chunlin said: "In antiquity Zheng favored Duke Shu and, for lack of instruction, was soon mocked; in Han the arrogant Prince of Li could not be tolerated to the end of his illness—these are recorded in the histories as warnings for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Chunlin wrote: "In antiquity, when Zheng favored a younger brother, lack of proper instruction brought swift reproach; in Han, an arrogant princely king could not be tolerated to the end—these lessons are recorded in history as warnings for all time.

sentences.zh: 二王性成英敏，休戚相關，料不至蹈覆轍，而慎終於始，要宜杜漸防微。

translations.literal: The two princes are by nature clever and keen, their weal and woe bound together; one expects they will not tread the old track, yet to be careful at the end one must begin with care—above all one should check the gradual and guard against the minute.
translations.idiomatic: The two princes are clever and keen by nature, and their fortunes are bound to the throne's; one expects they will not repeat past mistakes, yet care at the finish must begin at the start—above all, decline should be halted at its first signs.

sentences.zh: 」又謂：「景皇帝以神器付之皇上，衝齡踐阼，軍國重事，監國攝政王主之。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The Jing emperor entrusted the sacred vessel to our emperor; the throne was taken in tender years, and military and state affairs of weight are presided over by the regent prince.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote: "Emperor Jing entrusted the imperial mandate to our emperor, who ascended the throne in childhood; weighty military and state affairs are presided over by the regent prince.

sentences.zh: 治同其樂，亂同其憂，國之不保，家於何寄？

translations.literal: In order they share its joy, in disorder they share its sorrow—if the state is not preserved, upon what can the family rely?
translations.idiomatic: In peace they share its joy, in turmoil they share its sorrow—if the state is not preserved, what becomes of the clan?

sentences.zh: 」篇末又言：「監國歲未及週，物議沸騰，至於此極。

translations.literal: " At the end of the memorial he also said: "The regency has not yet reached a full year, yet public talk seethes to this extreme.
translations.idiomatic: " At the end of the memorial he added: "The regency has not yet completed a full year, yet public talk has already seethed to this pitch.

sentences.zh: 臣不禁為祖宗三百年國祚效賈生痛哭流涕長太息矣！

translations.literal: Your servant cannot but, for the three hundred years of our ancestors' imperial fortune, follow Jia Yi in weeping bitterly and sighing long!
translations.idiomatic: Your servant cannot but weep and sigh long, as Jia Yi did, for the three hundred years of our ancestors' imperial fortune!

sentences.zh: 」明年，又劾江西巡撫馮汝騤謾欺狀，效宋臣包拯七上彈章，末復言：「是非不明，請將前後章奏明詔宣示，敕部平議。
