translations.literal: " The next year he again impeached Feng Rukui, governor of Jiangxi, for deceitful conduct, following the Song minister Bao Zheng in submitting seven impeachment memorials; at the end he again said: "Right and wrong are unclear; I beg that the earlier and later memorials be proclaimed by clear edict and the ministries ordered to judge fairly.
translations.idiomatic: " The following year he impeached Feng Rukui, governor of Jiangxi, for deceitful conduct, following the Song minister Bao Zheng in submitting seven impeachment memorials; at the end he added: "Right and wrong remain unclear; I beg that all related memorials be proclaimed by clear edict and the ministries ordered to judge fairly.

sentences.zh: 」語至戇直，被訶責。

translations.literal: " His words were excessively blunt and he was rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: " His language was judged excessively blunt, and he was reprimanded.

sentences.zh: 复劾奕劻老奸竊位，多引匪人；

translations.literal: He again impeached Yikuang as an old traitor usurping office and bringing in many unworthy men;
translations.idiomatic: He again impeached Yikuang as a crafty old usurper of office who brought in many unworthy men;

sentences.zh: 非特簡忠良，不足以贊大猷、挽危局。

translations.literal: unless loyal and worthy men are specially selected, it will not suffice to assist the great plan or rescue a perilous situation.
translations.idiomatic: unless loyal and worthy men are specially selected, the great plan cannot be advanced nor a perilous situation rescued.

sentences.zh: 詞連尚書徐世昌，侍郎楊士琦、沈雲沛，總督陳夔龍、張人駿，巡撫寶棻、恩壽等十數人。

translations.literal: His words implicated more than a dozen men, including Ministers Xu Shichang, Vice Ministers Yang Shiqi and Shen Yunpei, Governors-General Chen Kuilong and Zhang Renjun, and Governors Bao Fen and Enshou.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial implicated more than a dozen officials, including Minister Xu Shichang, Vice Ministers Yang Shiqi and Shen Yunpei, Governors-General Chen Kuilong and Zhang Renjun, and Governors Bao Fen and Enshou.

sentences.zh: 朝旨再責之，令回原衙門行走。

translations.literal: The court again rebuked him and ordered him to return to his original office on reduced status.
translations.idiomatic: The court again rebuked him and ordered him back to his original office on reduced status.

sentences.zh: 春霖遂稱疾歸。

translations.literal: Chunlin then pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Chunlin then pleaded illness and retired home.

sentences.zh: 越八年，卒。

translations.literal: Eight years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Eight years later he died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：有清列帝，家法最嚴，迨至季世，創制垂簾，於是閹寺漸肆，而親貴權要亦聲勢日著，雖有直言敢諫之士，無補危亡，亦盡其心焉而已。

translations.literal: The historian comments: The successive emperors of Qing had the strictest household law; when the dynasty reached its late age and the innovation of holding the curtain arose, eunuchs gradually grew wanton and kinsmen and powerful favorites also daily grew conspicuous in influence; though there were men who spoke bluntly and dared remonstrate, they could not remedy peril and extinction—they only exhausted their hearts, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: The Qing emperors maintained the strictest household law; but in the dynasty's final age, with the innovation of regency from behind the curtain, eunuchs gradually grew brazen and princes and powerful favorites daily grew more conspicuous; though blunt-spoken remonstrators appeared, they could not stave off collapse—they could only give their utmost, and no more.

sentences.zh: 可讀屍諫，幸鑑孤忠。

translations.literal: Kedu remonstrated with his corpse; may his solitary loyalty be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Kedu remonstrated with his life; may his solitary loyalty be recognized.

sentences.zh: 一新、仁守、維峻先後直言，皆以語侵太后獲罪。

translations.literal: Yixin, Renshou, and Weijun spoke bluntly in turn and all were punished for words that offended the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin, Renshou, and Weijun spoke out in turn and all were punished for language that offended the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 文悌言攻結黨，實啟黨爭，而春霖連劾權貴，言尤痛切，當國者終於不悟。

translations.literal: Wen Ti's words attacked factionalism yet in fact opened factional strife; Chunlin repeatedly impeached the powerful, his words especially bitter, yet those who held the state never understood in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Ti attacked factionalism in word yet in fact helped open factional strife; Chunlin repeatedly impeached the powerful in especially bitter language, yet those who held power never understood.

sentences.zh: 又有太監寇連才，上書泣諫，請太后歸政，廢頤和園，且言：「不為祖宗天下計，獨不自為計？

translations.literal: There was also the eunuch Kou Liancai, who submitted a memorial weeping in remonstrance, asking the empress dowager to return power, abolish the Summer Palace, and saying: "If you do not plan for the ancestors' realm under Heaven, will you not even plan for yourself?
translations.idiomatic: There was also the eunuch Kou Liancai, who submitted a tearful memorial asking the empress dowager to return power and abolish the Summer Palace, writing: "If you will not plan for the realm our ancestors left, will you not even plan for yourself?

sentences.zh: 」終以違制被刑以死。

translations.literal: " In the end he was punished to death for violating regulations.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he was executed for violating regulations.

sentences.zh: 建言又何得以閹官少之？

translations.literal: How can remonstrance be slighted because the remonstrator was a eunuch?
translations.idiomatic: How can such remonstrance be belittled merely because the remonstrator was a eunuch?

sentences.zh: 類無可歸，故附見於此。

translations.literal: His kind had nowhere else to be placed, and so he is appended here.
translations.idiomatic: His case had no other proper place in the biographies, and so he is appended here.
